chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say:
It is disliked to exchange one wasq of dates from al-Madīnah for two wasqs of dates from Khaybar, because the dates of al-Madīnah are better in quality than the two.
He said: And he disliked that dates be sold for fresh dates immediately, with the same measure, to a term, because fresh dates dry out and thus decrease from their measure.

key_terms.أَجْوَدُهُمَا: Better in quality than the other.
key_terms.الرُّطَبِ: Fresh, moist dates that later dry and shrink.
key_terms.تَمْرِ الْمَدِينَةِ: Dates of al-Madīnah, mentioned here as being of superior quality.
key_terms.تَمْرِ خَيْبَرَ: Dates of Khaybar, used as the other commodity in the exchange.
key_terms.وَسْقًا: A dry measure used for agricultural goods such as dates.
key_terms.يَيْبَسُ: Dries out, causing reduction in volume.

ai.seo_question: Why is exchanging dates of different quality or selling dry dates for fresh dates disliked in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to exchanging dates of differing quality and condition, warning against forms of trade that lead to inequity in measured commodities. It highlights a legal concern connected to riba, especially where apparent equality in measure is undermined by differences in quality or by shrinkage over time.
